summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. She also reported transient chest discomfort, which was evaluated and ruled out as cardiac in origin. Imaging and lab studies showed no acute abnormalities, and stool tests were negative for bacterial, parasitic, and C. difficile infection, supporting a diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, including fluid rehydration and symptom management. She was maintained on her home cardiac and diabetes medications throughout admission and discharged home in good condition after resolution of symptoms, with instructions for follow-up and continuation of prescribed therapies.
